settings.heading: Description
settings.content: Rovina Sunglow delivers 12mg of natural astaxanthin in every softgel — one of the most powerful antioxidants found in nature. Sourced from Haematococcus pluvialis microalgae and paired with cold-pressed oil for absorption, it supports cellular defence, skin resilience and healthy inflammation response.*

settings.heading: Why do I need astaxanthin?
settings.content: Everyday stressors — sun exposure, screen time, hard training, air pollution — generate free radicals faster than the body can neutralise them. Astaxanthin sits inside the cell membrane and works on both its inner and outer surfaces, which is why it is studied so widely for cellular and skin support.*

settings.heading: Does it actually work?
settings.content: Astaxanthin is one of the better-studied carotenoids, with more than 70 published human clinical trials covering skin elasticity and moisture, eye fatigue, exercise recovery and cardiovascular markers. We formulated Sunglow at 12mg because that is the dose most of those trials used.*

settings.heading: Key ingredients
settings.content:
Natural astaxanthin (12mg) from Haematococcus pluvialis microalgae, grown in closed freshwater systems.

Cold-pressed olive oil as a lipid carrier, because astaxanthin is fat soluble and absorbs poorly on its own.

Vitamin E (as d-alpha tocopherol) to keep the formula stable without synthetic preservatives.

settings.heading: How do I take it?
settings.content: One softgel a day, with a meal that contains some fat. That is it. Consistency matters more than timing — most people notice the most after eight to twelve weeks of daily use.

settings.heading: Is it safe?
settings.content: Sunglow is made in a cGMP-certified facility in the USA and third-party tested for heavy metals, microbials and potency. It is non-GMO, gluten free and free from artificial fillers. If you are pregnant, nursing, or taking prescription medication, talk to your healthcare provider first.*

settings.heading: When will I see results?
settings.content: Astaxanthin builds up in tissue over time rather than acting on the first dose. Most customers report the first changes in skin feel and recovery around weeks three to four, with the fuller effect between weeks eight and twelve.*

settings.question: What is astaxanthin?
settings.answer: A red carotenoid produced by the microalgae Haematococcus pluvialis. It is what makes salmon and flamingos pink, and it is one of the most studied antioxidants available as a supplement.

settings.question: Why 12mg and not a lower dose?
settings.answer: Most published human trials on skin, eye and recovery outcomes used 6mg to 12mg per day. We formulated at the top of that range so you are taking the dose the research actually studied.*

settings.question: How long until I notice something?
settings.answer: Astaxanthin accumulates in tissue rather than acting immediately. Most people report the first changes between weeks three and four, and the fuller effect between weeks eight and twelve.*

settings.question: When should I take it?
settings.answer: One softgel a day with a meal that contains some fat. Timing does not matter much; consistency does.

settings.question: Can I take it with other supplements?
settings.answer: Yes. Astaxanthin pairs well with omega-3s and vitamin D. If you take prescription medication, check with your healthcare provider first.

settings.question: Is it vegan?
settings.answer: The astaxanthin is algae-derived, but the softgel casing is not vegan. A vegan capsule is on our roadmap.

settings.question: Are there any side effects?
settings.answer: Astaxanthin is well tolerated at this dose. A small number of people notice a slight orange tint to the skin at very high intakes, which is harmless and reverses when you stop.

settings.question: Is it third-party tested?
settings.answer: Every batch is tested by an independent lab for potency, heavy metals and microbials. Certificates of analysis are available on request.
